Stave Falls IS inside the City of Mission — unlike Dewdney-Deroche (FVRD Electoral Area G) and Lake Errock (FVRD Electoral Area C) in this batch. The City of Mission's own Rural Mission Strategy page names Stave Falls first among the rural communities it covers — "From Stave Falls, Steelhead and Silverdale to our other rural neighbourhoods" — and ties that work to the City's Official Community Plan. So City of Mission planning, zoning and tax rules are the relevant municipal frame here, and the rural-area (Province) tax regime does NOT apply.
Streets, schools and getting around Stave Falls

items.t: The page covers the Stave Falls community in the northern part of the City of Mission, around Stave Lake, Hayward Lake and the Stave River. Every first-page card was labelled with the board sub-area "Stave Falls" and a "Mission" mailing address (postal codes V4S 1xx), on streets including Wilson Street, Dewdney Trunk Road, Berg Avenue, Rolley Lake Street, Carr Street and Glacier Drive.

The name: "Stave Falls" is both the community name and the name of the falls/power site on the Stave River — BC Hydro's Powerhouse at Stave Falls, built in 1912, was once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source and is now a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and National Historic Site.

Stave Falls' specific OCP designation, zone names and the draft strategy's Stave Falls recommendations: Not verified pass — the City's site returned a bot-check page on direct fetch in that pass, and the strategy document itself was not opened.

The hydro system, from BC Hydro: a three-reservoir, three-generating-station system — water stored in Alouette Lake runs through Alouette Generating Station into Stave Lake, flows through the new powerhouse at Stave Falls into Hayward Lake, and finally through Ruskin Dam and Powerhouse before spilling into the Fraser River three kilometres south. The reservoirs are popular recreation areas; swimming, hiking, biking, fishing and boating are all options, and Hayward Lake in particular gets busy in summer. Any specific property's dock, moorage or water-access rights: Not verified.

Community park project: the City of Mission's engagement site covers a Stave Falls Community Park on Brackley Avenue, designed through a May 2023 community session beside the school, with entryways and park access from Brackley Avenue and the school. The park's built/opening status: Not verified — the engagement page describes design concepts and a survey that closed May 11, 2025.

Servicing, transit and health care: servicing (City water/sewer vs well/septic) for Stave Falls lots is not verified pass — the live feed's listing text repeatedly references drilled wells and septic systems on acreage lots, which is listing copy only. No TransLink or BC Transit service summary for Stave Falls was opened, no official source states commute times in minutes, and the nearest hospital on an official Fraser Health page is not verified in that pass.

The FVRD/Province frame used for Dewdney-Deroche and Lake Errock in this batch does NOT apply here.

Mission property taxes: Stave Falls properties are inside the City of Mission and pay municipal taxes to the City. City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with a flat 10% penalty on balances unpaid after July 2 — the City's tax page states: "A 10% penalty will be added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026." The flat 10% is the penalty under the Community Charter general tax collection scheme (ss. 233–234) as set by the Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s. 3; Mission has no alternative-scheme bylaw, and the rural-area penalty rules (5% + 5% to October 31, paid to the Province) do not apply inside the City.

The name and the hydro system: "Stave Falls" is both the community name and the name of the falls/power site on the Stave River. BC Hydro's Powerhouse at Stave Falls was built in 1912, was once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source, and remained in operation until a new powerhouse was built in 2000; the old powerhouse is now a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and National Historic Site. BC Hydro describes a three-reservoir, three-generating-station system — water stored in Alouette Lake runs through Alouette Generating Station into Stave Lake, flows through the new powerhouse at Stave Falls into Hayward Lake, and finally through Ruskin Dam and Powerhouse before spilling into the Fraser River.

Recreation: BC Hydro's Hayward Lake recreation area, near Mission on the Stave River system, is the area's anchor recreation site — the reservoir is an active hydroelectric facility and a popular recreation area, and the nearby Stave Lake boat launch and Ruskin Dam recreation area are also BC Hydro sites; the City of Mission restricts parking on city roads leading to Hayward Lake at busy times.
Nearby areas: Steelhead to the west/southwest, Mission West and Silverdale to the south, Ruskin and Hayward Lake across the Stave River side, and Durieu / the Hatzic Valley to the east.

Secondary suites and SSMUH: a Mission secondary suite is a self-contained living space inside a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; a suite is not a coach home or garden cottage (those are detached secondary dwellings); suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; all suites must be registered with the City, new suites go through the building permit process, and an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus utility fees applies. blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Stave Falls

items.t: Zoning — City of Mission Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020: Any Stave Falls parcel's actual zone: per-parcel, not verified.

Secondary suites and detached dwellings — Mission: a Mission secondary suite is a self-contained living space inside a single family home forming part of the same real estate entity; a suite is not a coach home or garden cottage (those are detached secondary dwellings); suites are not permitted in townhouses or rowhomes; all suites must be registered with the City, new suites go through the building permit process, and an annual secondary suite fee of $63 plus utility fees applies.

Property taxes — City of Mission (Stave Falls is city land, stated expressly): City of Mission 2026 property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026, with a FLAT 10% penalty added to any current balances outstanding (including unclaimed home owner grants) on July 3, 2026 (Community Charter ss.233–234 + Municipal Tax Regulation, B.C. Reg. 426/2003, s.3; Mission has NO alternative-scheme bylaw under Charter s.235). The FVRD rural regime — Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11, 5% after July 2 + 5% after October 31 — does NOT apply to a Stave Falls parcel; the two regimes are different and are never blended.

ALR block (applies where a Stave Falls parcel is ALR — status per-parcel, not verified here): subdivision within the ALR requires Agricultural Land Commission approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)). Caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). No ALR parcel count or split for Stave Falls is documented, and none is invented; check a parcel on the ALC maps.

blocks.text: Good to know about Stave Falls

items.t: The shoreline is a working hydro system, not a natural lakefront (BC Hydro, read Nov 1, 2026). BC Hydro's Powerhouse at Stave Falls was built in 1912, was once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source, and remained in operation until a new powerhouse was built in 2000; the old powerhouse is now a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and National Historic Site. The system runs Alouette Lake → Alouette Generating Station → Stave Lake → the new Stave Falls powerhouse → Hayward Lake → Ruskin Dam and Powerhouse → the Fraser River — so "waterfront" pricing must survive BC Hydro shoreline-tenure diligence, not just a view. Current (2026) Visitor Centre hours and admission prices are not verified (the BC Hydro source opened is a 2023 article).

Well and septic records are subject-removal items here (Nov 1, 2026). The feed's own listings run on drilled wells and septic systems; wells sit in the provincial GWELLS database, and sewerage systems must meet the Sewerage System Regulation's setbacks (including 30 m from a well unless professional advice is obtained) — pull both records on every deal, not in closing week.

Guide-only claims (the Powerhouse visitor centre closed/reopening-March-1-2027 status, Rolley Lake Provincial Park details, the Rural Mission Strategy approval date, Hayward Reservoir Trail lengths, the 12412 Bell Street rezoning package details, and the Hatzic Middle catchment assertion) are not verified site copy, not defects and not facts.

items.t: Board geography: “Stave Falls” is one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community “Mission” (Dewdney Deroche, Durieu, Hatzic, Hemlock, Lake Errock, Mission, Mission West, Stave Falls, Steelhead). Because Stave Falls is genuinely inside the City, Mission community figures apply as real community context here, not merely as a reporting grouping — still labelled community context only, never as acreage figures.

The name and the hydro system: “Stave Falls” is both the community name and the falls/power site on the Stave River — BC Hydro's Powerhouse at Stave Falls, built in 1912, was once B.C.'s biggest hydroelectric power source and is now a BC Hydro Visitor Centre and National Historic Site. BC Hydro describes a three-reservoir system: Alouette Lake → Alouette Generating Station → Stave Lake → new Stave Falls powerhouse → Hayward Lake → Ruskin Dam and Powerhouse → Fraser River three kilometres south. Reservoirs are used for swimming, hiking, biking, fishing and boating, with Hayward Lake busy in summer.
School in the community, Ministry-listed only: Stave Falls Elementary, 30204 Brackley Ave, Mission (SD75).

Local rules that affect duplexes in Stave Falls

items.t: Plan and zoning (Mission): Any parcel's actual zone is per-parcel: Not verified. Mission has no Supreme Court registry (mapping not verified). Lougheed Highway Corridor Plan: IN preparation, not adopted — Council endorsed Focused Land Use Option #2 on July 20, 2026.

ALR, wells, septic and the hydro shoreline: ALR status is per-parcel — check the ALC's ALR Property and Map Finder; on ALR parcels the ALC frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (≤40 ha) or 186 m² (>40 ha), and depositing a strata plan causes subdivision in the ALR and needs ALC permission (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s.6). Wells are recorded in the provincial gwells database, and onsite sewerage must comply with the Sewerage System Regulation, including the 30 m setback from a well unless professional advice is obtained. The shoreline is a working BC Hydro reservoir system (Alouette Lake → Stave Lake → Stave Falls powerhouse → Hayward Lake → Ruskin Dam): Any specific property's dock, moorage, shoreline-tenure or water-access rights are not verified.
